page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.large is a general purpose instance type built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.9 GHz. The instance delivers two dedicated virtual CPUs across one physical core using two hardware threads per core. Hardware specifications include 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), a 48 MB Level 3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The processor supports advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, requiring attached network-based block storage for persistent data disks.

Benchmark results demonstrate acceptable single-threaded compute efficiency alongside restricted multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests like Geekbench (1556.0) and stress-ng (1842.18) fall within the median range of comparable systems, supported by solid single-threaded compression and decompression throughput. However, overall parallel output is bounded by the single underlying physical core, leading to bottom-tier multi-core metrics in Geekbench (1815.0), PassMark CPU (2988.3), and clang compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained at 15.1 GB/sec for uncached reads and 13.63 GB/sec for writes, resulting in modest numbers for high-throughput memory operations such as Redis SET commands and large database operations.

From an operational and resource allocation perspective, ecs.g7se.large represents a cost-efficient entry point for environments requiring dedicated core isolation over burstable CPU models, avoiding CPU throttling risks. Due to the absence of integrated local NVMe storage and limited thread concurrency, the instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, including small-scale web servers, background task runners, CI/CD utility nodes, and development or staging environments with predictable execution demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.large is a general purpose compute instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. It provides two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, depending entirely on external cloud block storage. Benchmarks show solid single-core metrics across stress-ng and compression tasks, leveraging AVX-512 instruction sets. However, aggregate parallel throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit, as reflected in low multi-core PassMark, Geekbench, and Redis caching scores. Given the dedicated compute allocation and standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance without local storage overhead, the instance is an economical fit for lightweight web serving, microservices, continuous integration runners, and non-intensive general enterprise tasks.
